cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: (no config - demo: a fictional B2B SaaS company; every rate is an example input, not a benchmark)
THE ECONOMICS WORK - Referral costs less per customer than the channel it replaces, at these inputs.
400 customers -> 120 asked -> 30 refer -> 60 referrals -> 6 new customers
Saved vs other CAC  $2,400 this quarter
Combined rewards per referred customer can rise to $700 before referral costs as much as the channel it replaces.
Holding the friend reward, the referrer reward can be at most $550 per customer.
k = 0.015 new customers per existing customer per quarter; if referred customers refer at the same rate, each customer you win turns into 1.015 customers in total, itself included.

i  LTV is the same for referred and other customers. Research on a German bank found referred customers worth at least 16% more (Schmitt, Skiera and Van den Bulte, 2011), but that is a bank, not your product: measure your own referred cohort before you count on it.
i  These inputs are assumptions, not data: askedToReferrer, referralToCustomer. Treat every output as a scenario and replace them with measured rates after the first period.
* Orientation, not legal advice: These pointers name the rules AAJ's referral post covers. Check what they mean for your program with counsel before launch.

* FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR Part 255): Payment, free or discounted products and prize chances are treated as a "material connection" that must be disclosed when the audience would not expect it. If referrers post publicly to earn a reward, make the disclosure easy.
